pr_title: Support template light updating multiple attributes
pr_body:
<!--

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
This changes how template light works to support handling `light.turn_on` when both brightness and a color options are specified. This combines all of the set-value scripts into one `turn_on` script ~~that has varying attributes depending on what has changed~~. See #34915 for more info.

I think this solution is better than simply calling multiple scripts, as that could result in multiple API calls depending what the template light is controlling.

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The `set_level`, `set_temperature`, `set_color`, and `set_white_value` have become booleans to specify whether a light supports having these values set. Whenever the light is turned on, a single `turn_on` script is called instead of a different script for each case. If the light supports an attr, then the `turn_on` script will always receive the value. For example, if `set_level: true`, then `turn_on` will always receive `brightness`. ~~Additionally, if an attribute was specified in the service call, then its associate key like `brightness_new` will also be `True`.~~

## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box! 
  If your PR requires multiple boxes to be checked, you'll most likely need to
  split it into multiple PRs. This makes things easier and faster to code review.

- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml`:
<!--
  Supplying a configuration snippet, makes it easier for a maintainer to test
  your PR. Furthermore, for new integrations, it gives an impression of how
  the configuration would look like.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR does not have an example entry.
-->

```yaml
# Example configuration.yaml
- platform: template
  lights:
    example_light:
      friendly_name: "Example Light"
      level_template: "{{ states('input_number.light_example_level') | int }}"
      value_template: "{{ states('input_boolean.light_example_state') }}"
      color_template: "({{states('input_number.light_example_h') | int}},  {{states('input_number.light_example_s') | int}})"
      set_level: true
      set_color: true
      turn_on:
        # do some things to turn on.
        # Always receives the brightness and hs keys since set_level and set_color are true.
        # If one was specified in the service, then its _new key will be true, like brightness_new == True.
      turn_off:
        # do some things to turn off
```

Hey there @PhracturedBlue, @tetienne, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with a integration (`template`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L406) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I can understand the main issue. But I don't see why you removed the set_color, set_level, set_xxx services. How do you update an input number for instance when you change the light template color to red and how do you update another input number when you modify the brightness?
Perhaps a complete example can help.

@tetienne Thanks for the feedback. Here is an example that updates inputs for state, level, and color. This is the same as you would do with separate `set_xxx` functions but it all gets put into `turn_on`. This is how I am actually using it:
```yaml
# Example configuration.yaml
- platform: template
  lights:
    example_light:
      friendly_name: "Example Light"
      level_template: "{{ states('input_number.light_example_level') | int }}"
      value_template: "{{ states('input_boolean.light_example_state') }}"
      color_template: "({{states('input_number.light_example_h') | int}},  {{states('input_number.light_example_s') | int}})"
      set_level: true
      set_color: true
      turn_on:
          - service: input_boolean.turn_on
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_boolean.light_example_state
          - service: input_number.set_value
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_number.light_example_level
              value: "{{ brightness | int }}"
          - service: input_number.set_value
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_number.light_example_h
              value: "{{ h | int }}"
          - service: input_number.set_value
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_number.light_example_s
              value: "{{ s | int }}"
          - service: rest_command.update_my_light
             data_template:
                level: {{ states('input_number.light_example_level') | int }},
                h: {{ states('input_number.light_example_h') | int }},
                s: {{ states('input_number.light_example_s') | int }}
      turn_off:
          - service: input_boolean.turn_off
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_boolean.light_example_state
          - service: rest_command.update_my_light
             data_template:
                level: 0
```

Here is an example where having separate `set_xxx` function is not wanted. Obviously with the current bug, setting brightness and color simultaneously would not work, but if multiple `set_xxx` are called here then there will be multiple unnecessary HTTP requests (I know this doesn't apply to every case but the above fix allows for both separate or joined requests):
```yaml
- platform: template
  lights:
    example_light:
      friendly_name: "Example Light"
      level_template: "{{ states('input_number.light_example_level') | int }}"
      value_template: "{{ states('input_boolean.light_example_state') }}"
      color_template: "({{states('input_number.light_example_h') | int}},  {{states('input_number.light_example_s') | int}})"
      turn_on:
          - service: input_boolean.turn_on
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_boolean.light_example_state
          - service: rest_command.update_my_light
             data_template:
                level: {{ states('input_number.light_example_level') | int }},
                h: {{ states('input_number.light_example_h') | int }},
                s: {{ states('input_number.light_example_s') | int }}
      turn_off:
          - service: input_boolean.turn_off
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_boolean.light_example_state
          - service: rest_command.update_my_light
             data_template:
                level: 0
      set_level:
          - service: input_number.set_value
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_number.light_example_level
              value: "{{ brightness | int }}"
          - service: rest_command.update_my_light
             data_template:
                level: {{ states('input_number.light_example_level') | int }}
      set_color:
          - service: input_number.set_value
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_number.light_example_h
              value: "{{ h | int }}"
          - service: input_number.set_value
            data_template:
              entity_id: input_number.light_example_s
              value: "{{ s | int }}"
          - service: rest_command.update_my_light
             data_template:
                h: {{ states('input_number.light_example_h') | int }},
                s: {{ states('input_number.light_example_s') | int }}
```
Here is an example where if you _do_ require separate HTTP requests, you cans still do that with the new method:
```yaml
# Example configuration.yaml
- platform: template
  lights:
    example_light:
      friendly_name: "Example Light"
      level_template: "{{ states('input_number.light_example_level') | int }}"
      value_template: "{{ states('input_boolean.light_example_state') }}"

              entity_id: input_number.light_example_level

          - service: input_number.set_value

          - service: rest_command.update_my_light

             data_template:

```

I think the PR is good in general. Only question is the breaking change. Should we be backwards compatible or not?

Test were failing because `hs` often returns `None`, but for some reason that I cannot figure out, this value was now being rounded in `LightEntity` (can't figure out why this wasn't happening before, [as that was added long before this pull but it just wasn't happening](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blame/dev/homeassistant/components/light/__init__.py#L446)).

There were two tests that failed:
 - A test that sees the default type of the entity when it is created
 - A test that sets the template to `{{ none }}` and expects to get `None` out as the value (this test was written before this pull)

I am inclined to think that the entity should be modified to allow for these values to be `None`, as it seemed to have in the past, and some other change not to the `LightEntity` caused this issue to appear. It would also be unexpected to set the template to `{{ none }}` and get back `(0, 0)`. It would further be unexpected behavior for when the template initializes all of the other attributes (i.e. brightness) to be `None` but hs to be `(0, 0)`. This would also be consistent with the other templates, which initialize all of their attributes to `None`.

I have pushed a commit to fix this; let me know if I should remove it or fix it a different way.

I have not thought about if this issue is relevant if this is steered to not be a breaking change, so maybe that should be decided first.

Now back to the breaking change issue:

I'm not sure how to keep both solutions without the docs (and code) becoming extremely confusing. In the new case, the `turn_on` script is always used. However, in the old case, `turn_on` was not always called. So we would have to rename the "new" `turn_on` and all of the other new boolean attributes to something new, which would be confusing for someone trying to move away from the deprecated method, as you would still be able to define the new `turn_on` with an older individual calls like `set_level`.

But that also seems less ideal because I'm not sure what else to call it other than `turn_on_new`, which shouldn't be a permanent attribute name. 

TLDR: the new `turn_on` is not backwards compatible, so it would have to be renamed to something else. The other attributes could theoretically be modified to accept either a boolean or a script. However, this allows for strange combinations of old and new.

I think we can stay backwards compatible if we validate the changed options to either all be of type boolean or all `cv.Script`, if set. We can add a custom validator that does this. Then we can check if the user wants the legacy pattern or the new pattern.

If only the turn_on option is used we just send an empty dict as script variables. That's the default anyway, so there's no effective change.

Please don't let this stale.

Also, because of the fact that you cannot specify brightness and color in the same time, the scenes configuration becomes larger than they should.

@DaAwesomeP do you have any workaround for google assistant? Can we use this as a custom component or something like that if this doesn't integrate in the end?

issue_context.title: Template Light Does Not Update Multiple Attributes
issue_context.body:
## The problem
Quite simply, this should probably not be an if/else if/else block: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/template/light.py#L335-L354 (however this is more complicated to fix, see Additional Notes section)

Running the `turn_on` service with a Template Light and multiple attributes does not set all of the attributes.
```yaml
# These examples require a Template Light with set_color and set_level (see code block later in issue)
# This sets only brightness (despite color also specified)
- service: light.turn_on
  data:
    entity_id: light.room1_color_lights
    color_name: red
    brightness: 76.5

# This sets only color (as expected)
- service: light.turn_on
  data:
    entity_id: light.room1_color_lights
    color_name: red

# This sets only brightness(as expected)
- service: light.turn_on
  data:
    entity_id: light.room1_color_lights
    brightness: 76.5
```

## Environment
- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.109.0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): Unknown
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): HassOS 3.13 w/ Supervisor 219
- Integration causing this issue: Template Light
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light.template/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```yaml
- platform: template
  lights:
    example_light:
      friendly_name: "Example Light"
      level_template: "{{ states('input_number.light_example_level') | int }}"
      value_template: "{{ states('input_boolean.light_example_state') }}"
      color_template: "({{states('input_number.light_example_h') | int}},  {{states('input_number.light_example_s') | int}})"
      turn_on:
        # do some things to turn on
      turn_off:
        # do some things to turn off
      set_level:
        # do some things to set the brightness
      set_color:
        # do some things to set the color

```

## Traceback/Error logs
No relevant logs present.

## Additional information
I think this is more complicated to fix than it may initially seem. With the current design of Template Light, the `set_*` functions make calls to change each attribute. In my particular use case, I have an RGB light controlled via HTTP, and calling multiple of these functions would send multiple successive HTTP calls (not ideal).

A possible solution would be to mimic how it works in the service and have only `turn_on` and `turn_off` scripts available to set in YAML. All of the attributes set would be sent to `turn_on` and the user would have to use templating to figure out which attributes are set and which are not being updated. I suppose it is more difficult on the user-end, but then multiple attributes can be updated simultaneously and efficiently.

Another method would be to add an `apply` script option that would run after the `set_*` functions to apply the changes setup by the `set_*` functions, but that seems much more complicated for the user to implement.
